what_its_for: This medicine is used to treat nausea and vomiting, and it is also used to treat symptoms of certain mental health conditions such as schizophrenia. It works by blocking certain chemical signals in the brain that cause nausea or contribute to mental health symptoms.
how_to_take: Take this medicine exactly as your doctor tells you. It comes in different forms including tablets, extended-release capsules, rectal suppositories, and injectable forms given by a healthcare provider. Swallow tablets whole with a full glass of water. You may take it with food or milk if it upsets your stomach. Do not crush or chew extended-release capsules. If you are using a suppository, follow the instructions provided by your pharmacist. Do not take more than prescribed.
dosing: For nausea and vomiting in adults, the usual dose is 5 to 10 mg taken 3 to 4 times per day, or as directed by your doctor. For extended-release capsules, the usual dose is 15 to 30 mg once daily in the morning. Your doctor will choose the right dose and form based on your condition, age, weight, and other health factors. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do not take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one. If you are unsure what to do, call your doctor or pharmacist.
storage: Store tablets and capsules at room temperature between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep the medicine away from heat, direct light, and moisture. Do not store in the bathroom. Keep suppositories refrigerated between 36°F and 46°F (2°C to 8°C). Keep all forms of this medicine out of reach of children and pets. Do not use the medicine past the expiration date on the label. Ask your pharmacist how to safely dispose of unused medicine.
what_to_avoid: Avoid drinking alcohol while taking this medicine, as it can increase drowsiness and dizziness. Avoid driving, operating heavy machinery, or doing anything that requires you to be alert until you know how this medicine affects you. Avoid getting overheated or becoming dehydrated, especially in hot weather or during exercise, as this medicine can affect your body's ability to regulate temperature. Avoid prolonged sun exposure and use sunscreen when going outdoors, as this medicine can make your skin more sensitive to sunlight. Avoid taking antacids or anti-diarrhea medicines within 2 hours of taking prochlorperazine, as they may reduce its effectiveness. Tell your doctor about all other medicines, vitamins, and supplements you take, as many drugs can interact with this medicine.
when_to_call_doctor: Contact your doctor right away if you experience any of the following: uncontrollable movements of your face, tongue, or body (called tardive dyskinesia); severe muscle stiffness or rigidity, high fever, confusion, or sweating (signs of a serious reaction called neuroleptic malignant syndrome); unusual restlessness or inability to sit still; severe dizziness or fainting; fast, irregular, or pounding heartbeat; difficulty breathing or swallowing; yellowing of your skin or eyes (jaundice); unusual bruising or bleeding; seizures; signs of low blood pressure such as lightheadedness when standing up; painful or prolonged erection (in males); or signs of a serious allergic reaction such as rash, swelling of the face or throat, or difficulty breathing. Also call your doctor if your nausea or vomiting does not improve or gets worse.
when_it_works: For nausea and vomiting, this medicine usually starts working within 30 to 60 minutes after taking it by mouth. For mental health conditions, it may take several days to a few weeks of regular use before you notice the full benefit. Do not stop taking this medicine suddenly without talking to your doctor, even if you feel better.
special_populations: Children: This medicine should generally not be used in children under 2 years of age or weighing less than 20 pounds (about 9 kg). Use with caution in children, and only as directed by a doctor. Elderly patients: Older adults are more sensitive to the side effects of this medicine, especially drowsiness, dizziness, low blood pressure, and movement problems. Lower doses are often used in elderly patients. Pregnancy: Talk to your doctor before using this medicine if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant. Use near the time of delivery may cause movement problems or withdrawal symptoms in newborns. Breastfeeding: This medicine may pass into breast milk. Talk to your doctor about the risks and benefits before breastfeeding. Liver or kidney problems: Let your doctor know if you have liver or kidney disease, as dose adjustments may be needed.
